gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
gaps.explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

gaps.sentence: 'The delay is your fault,' the manager said to her. The manager ___ her for the delay.
gaps.explanation: Blame takes the pattern blame somebody for something.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
"Do not touch the wire!" — She warned me ___ the wire.
gaps.explanation: 'Warn somebody not to do' — 'not' comes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.
